display.title: Episode 485: The Lost Wallet (Yud-Gimmel Tammuz)
display.summary_short: On Yud-Gimmel Tammuz, Uncle Yossi recalls the Frierdiker Rebbe's miraculous release, then tells of a poor yeshiva boy who returned a bank president's wallet and found his family's fortune.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Yud-Gimmel Tammuz. Uncle Yossi explains why the twelfth and thirteenth of Tammuz are days of thanksgiving and good resolutions: in 1927 the Frierdiker Rebbe was sentenced for gathering Jewish children to teach them Torah, and was miraculously freed, later building a worldwide network of yeshivos. He prays that this redemption lead to the final Geulah. After the Hakochainik march, a boy visiting from Madrid, Spain says the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. The story is about hashavas aveidah. Little Dovid, who has just learned the mitzvah in yeshiva, finds a wallet with twelve hundred dollars. He wins the struggle between his yetzer tov and yetzer hara, and with his sick, widowed mother he arranges to return it to the bank president who lost it. Visiting their poor home, the banker learns that Dovid's late father was the generous man who once lent him the money that made his fortune, and he has been saving the share he owes them ever since. The family's troubles are over, all because Dovid returned what he found.
display.lesson: Always return what you find to its owner; being honest when no one is looking brings Hashem's blessing.

date.note: 'Today is Yud-Gimmel Tammuz'; the year is called 'the year of wonders' (5751); one week after episode 484. A Tuesday.

advisories.note: The Frierdiker Rebbe was sentenced to death for teaching Torah to children and miraculously freed.
A widowed mother and her son live in poverty until the happy ending.
The boy's mother is bedridden and cannot afford a doctor; the boy's father died of an illness.

privacy.note: Shema guest named in full, with his home city.

sources_cited.note: 'Lismoch geulah ligeulah', linking one redemption to the next, cited as what the Chachamim teach.
